counterfactual_missing_items: No candidate explicitly links the thrombus to the bicuspid aortic valve and ascending aortic aneurysm as a composite diagnosis
R8 label does not state the left coronary ostial obstruction, though the raw span includes it
No raw span uses the word 'occlusion'; 'covering most' and 'slow perfusion' are inferential
decisive_items: Organized thrombus measuring 1 × 0.8 cm found at the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve, covering most of the left coronary artery's ostium
Confirmed the excised mass as an organized thrombus
Demonstrated slow blood perfusion in the left coronary artery, without evidence of significant atherosclerosis
response.rationale: R8 is the primary histopathologically confirmed lesion: an organized thrombus on the aortic valve at the left coronary cusp. R7 captures the downstream slow coronary perfusion and ostial coverage but labels the process as coronary artery occlusion rather than the valve thrombosis that is the actual excised mass. C2/C3 are correlated append-only completions that add anatomy already present in R8's raw span; R6/R4/R1 and their completions describe associated aortopathy/valve findings but not the acute symptomatic lesion.

rejected.why: Describes the coronary flow consequence but mislocates the primary thrombotic process to the coronary artery rather than the aortic valve cusp.
Correlated append-only completion of R7; adds anatomy already present in the intraoperative span but still frames the diagnosis as coronary occlusion rather than valve thrombosis.
Correlated append-only completion of R8; adds left coronary cusp to the label but the parent R8 raw span already contains that location, so no new raw evidence.
Ascending aortic aneurysm is a true imaging finding but does not explain the thrombus, coronary slow perfusion, or syncope.
Append-only completion of R6 adding measurements; same limitation as R6 and no link to the acute thrombotic lesion.
Bicuspid aortic valve is an associated congenital finding but not the acute symptomatic diagnosis; does not account for the thrombus or coronary ostial coverage.
Append-only completion of R4 adding mild regurgitation; still lacks the thrombotic lesion and coronary consequence.
Composite of bicuspid valve and aneurysm, but omits the definitive thrombus and ostial obstruction that explain the presentation.
Adds mild regurgitation to R1; still omits the thrombus and coronary ostial obstruction, so incomplete for the acute diagnosis.
